Formulation:

- Protective factors: Patient engaged with care, willing to follow treatment plan

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Migraine with aura
- Patient Goal(s): Relief of headache and associated symptoms; reduce anxiety about diagnosis; return to normal functioning
- Clinical Goal(s): Symptomatic control of migraine episodes; monitor for neurological signs; provide reassurance and education regarding migraine
- Actions (Patient): Take recommended medications (ibuprofen and antiemetics as advised); avoid activities that exacerbate symptoms; attend follow-up assessment
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Recommend and provide migraine-specific medications (ibuprofen, antiemetics, doses to be clarified); arrange follow-up neurological examination; provide reassurance regarding differential diagnoses; educate about migraine and symptom management; monitor for any new neurological symptoms requiring urgent evaluation

Secondary Problem: Health anxiety/hypochondriasis related to headache symptoms
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce health-related anxiety and distress; enhance coping strategies
- Clinical Goal(s): Address anxiety through appropriate support and education; monitor impact on mental wellbeing
- Actions (Patient): Engage in discussions about concerns; practice coping strategies provided
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide reassurance; consider referral to psychological support if anxiety persists or worsens; educate patient about early warning signs that warrant urgent care

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Migraine symptoms and typical course; need for medication adherence; when to seek urgent medical attention; reassurance about symptoms and differential diagnoses
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: New neurological deficits (weakness, gait disturbance), sudden worsening visual symptoms, unrelenting severe headache, fever or neck stiffness
- Coping Strategies: Avoid excessive movement during attacks; use medications as directed; limit screen exposure to reduce photophobia; seek support for health anxiety concerns

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Not explicitly documented but implied by engagement
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None recorded
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: Follow-up neurological evaluation scheduled (date not specified)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Migraine with aura: High likelihood; typical unilateral headache with visual aura, nausea, vomiting, family history supportive
- Stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA): Medium likelihood; sudden onset headache and visual changes but no neurological deficits reduces probability
- Meningitis or encephalitis: Low likelihood; headache, vomiting, photophobia possible but absence of fever or neck stiffness reduces likelihood
